Add AHRQ Elixhauser comorbidity columns (experimental)

Source: R/comorbidity.R
nis_comorbidity.Rd

Reshapes the wide I10_DX1, I10_DX2, ... columns of a collected data frame to one row per code, hands them to medicalcoder::comorbidities(), and joins the result back in the original row order. All code-to-condition mapping and index weights come from the medicalcoder package, which ships the AHRQ Elixhauser Comorbidity Software Refined for ICD-10-CM tables; easyNIS holds no clinical code lists. Install it with install.packages("medicalcoder").

Usage

nis_comorbidity(.data, method = "elixhauser_ahrq_icd10", prefix = "cmrb_")

Arguments

.data

A collected data frame with I10_DX1, I10_DX2, ... columns, or a tbl_svy from nis_design() that kept them. Lazy DuckDB queries are not accepted; call dplyr::collect() first.

method

A medicalcoder Elixhauser method name. The default, "elixhauser_ahrq_icd10", is the union of every ICD-10 code AHRQ has listed since FY2022, which suits NIS years pooled across code-set updates. Use "elixhauser_ahrq2022" through "elixhauser_ahrq2026" to pin one AHRQ release.

prefix

Prefix for the added columns. Existing columns are never replaced.

Value

.data with one logical column per condition (<prefix>hf, ...), <prefix>n (conditions flagged), <prefix>any, and the integer <prefix>mortality_index and <prefix>readmission_index scores, using the names and weights from medicalcoder. Rows with no usable I10_DX* code are NA in all of them; see the Assumptions section.

Details

The function is experimental: the default method and the assumptions below remain pending scientific approval.

Assumptions

  • Present on admission is approximated. NIS includes diagnosis POA fields (DXPOA1, DXPOA2, and so on), but this helper does not use them. It passes every diagnosis as present on admission (poa = 1L). AHRQ's refined Elixhauser method requires POA for 18 of its 38 measures, so this approximation can count a complication that arose during the stay as pre-existing for a POA-sensitive measure.

  • Principal diagnosis is I10_DX1. It is passed as the primary diagnosis, and medicalcoder applies the AHRQ rule for it (for example, a condition is not flagged from the principal diagnosis alone where AHRQ excludes it). Codes in I10_DX2 onward are secondary.

  • ICD-10 only. Only the I10_DX* columns are read. A discharge with no usable I10_DX* code (all blank, missing or invalid UTF-8), such as an ICD-9 discharge from before October 2015, gets NA in every added column, and the function warns with the number of such rows. Do not treat those NA values as "no comorbidity".

  • Codes are upper-cased with periods and spaces removed. Blank, missing or invalid UTF-8 codes are ignored, and an unmapped code adds no condition. A discharge with at least one usable but unmapped code gets zeros.

  • The long reshaping holds about 40 diagnosis columns by every row in memory. Use it on a cohort, not on the full national file.

Differences from the Stata-derived columns

NIS studies often already carry ynel* indicators and elixsum, derived in Stata from an earlier Elixhauser release. They are not reproduced here and should not be expected to agree: the AHRQ Refined software uses different condition definitions and categories (for example, hypertension with and without heart failure or renal failure, and separate liver, neurological and cancer subtypes), POA-dependent flagging, and the principal-diagnosis rule above. Do not mix the two sets of indicators in one model.

Use with nis_design()

nis_design() needs the whole hospital-year frame to build placeholder rows, so do not collect and enrich the cohort before calling it. Keep the diagnosis columns in the design instead, then pass the design here:

design <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = c(AGE, starts_with("I10_DX")))
design <- nis_comorbidity(design)

For a tbl_svy the function replaces design$variables and leaves the design (clusters, strata, weights) untouched.

See also

Comorbidity indicators.

Examples

discharges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  dplyr::select(AGE, dplyr::starts_with("I10_DX")) |>
  dplyr::collect()
